e7_s4_rationale: The presence of a hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts, proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, and a well-circumscribed papule with a flakier surface at one lateral end are characteristic features of verrucous carcinoma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: While squamous cell carcinoma can present with similar features, the well-circumscribed nature and hyperkeratotic appearance of the lesion, along with the presence of pseudohorn cysts, are more typical of verrucous carcinoma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma typically has a more rapid growth phase and often resolves on its own, which does not match the 4-year history of the lesion in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ with invasive components
e7_s4_rejected.why: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures, suggests invasive carcinoma, but the overall appearance is more consistent with verrucous carcinoma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with clear cell features
e7_s4_rejected.why: While the lesion does have clear cell features, the overall clinical and histopathological picture is more consistent with verrucous carcinoma, which can also exhibit clear cell changes.
